summary: Sampling PC profiler for the ARM cores and the 6809 guest
description: Requested so the firmware session can see where the guest 6809 program spends its time; the emulator had nothing that recorded PCs. Implemented in commit 9fe8a56 (pushed to ugufru/cocozero-emulator main): src/profiler.rs, hooked into CoCoZeroSoC::step_cycles (src/soc.rs), flags in src/main.rs: --profile <file>, --profile-interval <cycles> (default 10000), --profile-6809-offsets CPU_PTR,REG_PC (default 340,88). When profiling is off, step_cycles runs exactly the code it ran before. ARM side: samples both Cortex-M33 PCs and groups them by function from the firmware ELF (--elf, else roms/cocozero.elf, the same rule as src/symbols.rs). Verified on headless runs; e.g. core 1 is 99% in dvi_static_framebuf_main_16bpp. 6809 side: the 6809 is XRoar's struct MC6809 in firmware SRAM, not something this emulator models. The PC is read by pointer chase: g_m (static CocoMachine in the firmware's lib/coco_machine/src/coco_machine.cpp, ELF symbol _ZL3g_m or g_m) -> .cpu at +340 -> .reg_pc (uint16) at +88. The ELF has no DWARF for these structs, so the offsets were read off the disassembly: mc6809_get_pc is `ldrh r0, [r0, #88]`, and loads of g_m.cpu use #340. That agrees with a hand layout of CocoMachine and holds for both roms/cocozero.elf and the firmware's pizero_stream_60 build as of 2026-10-12. NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE: in every run the guest never started, because the virtual SD card (./coco) has no Color BASIC ROMs; core 0 sits in timer_busy_wait_until on a boot page (coco_boot_card_present shows in the samples) and the report shows every sample as 'before the 6809 existed'. To close: put ROMs in coco/roms, run e.g. `cargo run --release -- --headless --max-frames 1500 --profile prof.txt`, and confirm the 6809 section lists plausible Color BASIC addresses (e.g. the keyboard polling loop at the OK prompt). Known limit: the PC is sampled between emulator slices, so it can land mid-instruction; fine for hot spots, not exact per-instruction attribution. Follow-ups filed as EMU-04, EMU-05, EMU-06.

summary: symbols tests hard-code addresses from an older firmware
description: src/symbols.rs tests test_elf_symbol_parsing (around line 240) and test_flash_signature_scanning (around line 261) assert fixed addresses (fb 0x20022900, menu_active 0x2000c8d0, ...) that matched an earlier firmware. Upstream commit 6305096 'update: latest firmware for cocozero' replaced roms/cocozero.elf and .uf2, and those addresses moved (the current ELF gives fb=0x20022780, menu=0x2000C8E8, hid_cb=0x1001F3A4). Confirmed failing on unmodified upstream main in a temporary worktree, so it was not caused by EMU-01. Fix: either update the constants, or better, assert that ELF parsing and flash-signature scanning agree with each other, so the tests survive future firmware drops. The FirmwareSymbols::default() fallback values in the same file are equally stale.

Fails on current main and also on unmodified upstream main (6305096), checked in a temporary worktree, so it predates EMU-01. Cause not investigated. Likely related to EMU-02: the menu addresses moved with the firmware update, and the test or the menu detection in src/soc.rs may depend on the stale values. Also possible: like EMU-01, the menu may need ROMs on the virtual SD card to be reachable. Start by running `cargo test --release --test menu_test -- --nocapture`.

summary: Profiler: name 6809 addresses (Color BASIC / Extended BASIC labels)
description: The 6809 section of the --profile report (src/profiler.rs, Profiler::report) lists raw $XXXX addresses. Add an optional symbol map so ROM routines show by name, e.g. a simple 'ADDR NAME' text file passed via a flag, plus a range-to-name lookup like ElfSymbols::func_at. Possible sources for Color BASIC labels: published disassemblies, or the analyze-rom skill. Depends on EMU-01 being verified live first.

summary: Profiler: write full sample counts as CSV
description: The --profile report shows only the top 50 rows per section (TOP_N in src/profiler.rs) and folds the rest into one line. Write the full histograms (core, address, symbol, count; and 6809 address, count) to a CSV beside the report, so other tools and sessions can post-process them, e.g. aggregate by 6809 page or diff two runs.

summary: Profiler: derive 6809 PC offsets from the ELF instead of hard-coding
description: DEFAULT_CPU_PTR_OFFSET (340) and DEFAULT_REG_PC_OFFSET (88) in src/profiler.rs are constants read off one firmware's disassembly (see EMU-01). If the firmware adds a field to CocoMachine or builds MC6809 with TRACE defined (which inserts trace fields before the registers in lib/xroar_core/src/mc6809/mc6809.h), the profiler silently samples the wrong word. Derive them from the ELF: decode the Thumb-2 `ldrh.w r0, [r0, #imm]` at the mc6809_get_pc symbol for reg_pc, and find a reliable accessor for g_m.cpu (or ask the firmware session to export a small accessor or fixed-layout descriptor). At minimum, add a sanity check: warn if the sampled 6809 PCs never change, or never fall inside ROM/RAM ranges.
